title: The Car Ride
summary: Three POVs in the same car — or rather, two in the car and one waiting outside. Zoey is starving but won't touch the snacks. Mira keeps correcting her posture and hating herself for it. Rumi has spent a morning researching optimal snacks for Seoul teenagers aged 16–24 and found no reliable data. She is outside anyway.
key_beats: Zoey: flashback to the hotel minibar — the snacks she ate during her parents' fight, the bill, the double scolding.
Mira: knows the car from Appa. Can't stop sitting up straight. Hates herself for it.
Rumi: settled on Honey Butter Chips, choco pies, gummies. Cannot eat any of them. Does not regret the research.
Celine has asked Rumi to wait inside three times. Rumi is outside.
tone: Anxious warmth. Three people preparing for the worst who are about to be surprised.

title: Annyeonghaseyo
summary: They arrive. Rumi is standing precisely in the centre of the courtyard. Zoey's first words are that the house is so quiet you could get murdered there. This is not the first-impression she was going for.
key_beats: Rumi has made binders. Colour-coded. Cross-referenced. Personalised cartoon graphics.
Zoey: bowing anxiety. She has bowed at Chuseok her whole life. This time it matters, so she's terrified of doing it wrong.
Mira: the compelled greeting is right there in her throat. Eomma's words. She will not say them. Stays silent. Zoey fills the gap by accident.
Rumi responds to the murder comment with a genuine security threat analysis. Celine's eye twitches.
Tour: seven comfort trees rated in order. The chinese hackberry has sub-optimal back support. The full 23-tree rating is available on request.
objects: Blue binder (capybara in bath of oranges)
tone: Awkward and tender. All three of them trying so hard.

title: House Rules
summary: Mira opens the binder expecting rules to follow. Finds information given for their comfort. Has to revise her threat assessment of Rumi entirely.
key_beats: Rumi chose blue for Zoey after finding a survey. The survey was not published in a peer-reviewed journal.
Mira's internal wall goes up at the word 'binders'. Comes down slowly as she reads.
Zoey fills silence with thirty seconds of green-colour thoughts. Cuts herself off. Mira watches, relieved.
The binder has cartoon frogs, bears, and butterflies. Personalised per girl. Mira wants to know why she got the panda.
Revelation: no hidden rules. No secret ways to fail. No one is trying to catch her out.
tone: Mira's defences meeting something that doesn't push back.

title: The Kitchen
summary: Mugs and meal rules. Mira pushes on the mug question not to cause trouble, but because things need to make sense. Rumi's mug is chipped. Mira doesn't know this yet.
key_beats: The mugs all look identical. Rumi's is chipped — she doesn't want anyone cut, can't throw it out.
Mira keeps asking. Zoey fidgets nervously. Rumi is confused, not annoyed.
Mira backs down when she sees Zoey's anxiety. Decides the question isn't worth it.
Meals at 7, 1, and 8:30. Also: help yourself between meals if you're hungry.
Mira has never, ever lived anywhere with that rule. Not home, not relatives, not boarding school, not the 'supported educational facility'.
objects: Oso berries and Islay — fruits native to California Celine refused to order
tone: Small kindnesses landing hard on someone who has never received them casually.

title: Being an Example
summary: Rumi on the strange new world of living with people her own age. She loves it. She also sometimes wants them to be a bit less present.
key_beats: For the first time, Rumi is part of something Celine isn't part of. The word 'you girls' sends a tingle through her every time.
She is an example to be followed. Watch Rumi. See how Rumi does it. She could get used to this.
The new rules of conversation: say things even when you have nothing to say. Ask questions. Don't ask too many. Remember what they said. Ask Celine to write this down. Celine says no.
The notebook. Byeol comparison. Rumi understands the comparison. Does not understand the reasoning. Hides the notebook.
Zoey's stuffed animals: lounging on the bed, thrown at Mira during the shark documentary, entirely not put away.
Celine praises Mira's uppercut. Rumi is being held up as the standard. Mira is almost grounding that standard. It burns.
tone: Rumi trying very hard to be generous and not entirely managing it. And being honest about this to herself.

title: The Quiet
summary: Zoey on the compound. The compound is quiet. No one yells. She has her own room, no one needs to know about the rest.
key_beats: No yelling. No slamming. No pointed huffing. No plates put down too hard. This is a surprise.
She is not brave. She was picked last in gym class since third grade. She has said this to Celine repeatedly. Celine's response: 'I know what I'm doing, Zoey.'
Mira is different. Zoey was prepared to spend every second of every day seething at how effortlessly she moves. Luckily, Mira is herself.
The warmth she feels watching Mira succeed in training. The cheerleaders at the football game. This is the same warmth.
Rumi caught her with Sol. She froze. Then Mira said 'it's cute' and the moment passed.
Mira keeps bringing up Sol. It's ok. You don't have to hide. She holds onto that.
The phone call home. Her mother's reminders. Mira sets up camp at the other end of the table without explanation.
'Cat amongst the pigeons'. Mira's face. Twenty-five minutes later, a hug, a kiss on both cheeks. 'Seriously, I don't know what I would have done without you.'
tone: Zoey slowly, cautiously realising that maybe it will be ok.

title: Byeol
summary: Zoey comes to Rumi's room to see it for the first time. Finds Byeol. He rips.
key_beats: Free time. Zoey follows Rumi down the hall and into her room. Rumi is not sure why.
Rumi watching Zoey spin in happy circles. It makes her dizzy. She can't look away.
'A packrat?' — 'A hoarder?' — Zoey's smile dims. Her mum's word.
Byeol. Five years hidden in the closet. No one has touched him in all that time.
The snatching. The tearing sound. The sawdust.
He is ruined. This is fine. It is right that he is ruined. She is an example. This is how it should be.
She bites her lip until she tastes blood in the studio. It is fine. Her eyes sting. It is fine.
It is not fine.
tone: The quiet devastation of someone telling themselves they are fine.

title: Zoey Knows One Person Who Might
summary: Zoey stands in Rumi's room looking at what she's done and knows she cannot fix it alone. She runs to Mira.
key_beats: Byeol on the floor. Evidence of Zoey's eternal life-ruining Zoey-ness.
Rumi takes a broken nose without flinching. That look on her face was something else.

The nose incident in full: Mira's panic, Rumi's genuine confusion, Zoey fetching the towel, Celine sweeping in. 'I landed badly.' Mira didn't. Rumi covering for her without being asked, because Mira looked like she didn't want Celine to know.
The peanut butter campaign: Rumi lobbying for a food she is severely allergic to. 'I thought it was worth asking.'
She can't fix this. She knows someone who might.
She runs to Mira's room.
objects: The dining table ice pack conversation
tone: Zoey in the aftermath. Spiralling, then choosing to act.

title: One More Thing
summary: Mira opens the door expecting Celine and finds Zoey crying. She nods yes before she hears the question. They repair Byeol.
key_beats: Mira's first thought at a knock: magazine, not trouble. She is proud of this.
She nods yes before Zoey explains. Of course she will help. Who wouldn't.
Antique. Sawdust. Worn-thin fabric. She has never been resigned to this.
The sewing skill: alteration after alteration during the eating disorder. Clothes that no longer fit. Confiscation of materials. Six months in the 'supported educational facility'.
Zoey's eyes drift to Sol. Then to Mira's. Neither of them brave enough to touch Celine's property.
Zoey cuts open Sol's flipper with the sewing scissors. No hesitation. 'I don't mind if Sheldon's different now.'
The bear is smaller in one place. A little mismatched. The best that she, or anyone, could do.
One more thing before they go to Rumi.
tone: Mira at her most quietly heroic. Determined. Doing the thing she is actually, genuinely, really good at.
